title: English Vocabulary Builder
description: Expand your English vocabulary with commonly used words

questions.question: What does 'ubiquitous' mean?
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous means present, appearing, or found everywhere. It describes something that seems to be in all places at the same time.

questions.question: What is an 'antonym'?
choices: A word with the same meaning
A word with the opposite meaning
A word that sounds the same
A word borrowed from another language
questions.explanation: An antonym is a word that has the opposite meaning of another word. For example, 'hot' and 'cold' are antonyms.

questions.question: What does 'meticulous' mean?
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. A meticulous person pays close attention to small details.

questions.question: What does 'ambiguous' mean?
choices: Having more than one possible meaning
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning. It describes something unclear or uncertain.

questions.question: What is a 'palindrome'?
choices: A word that reads the same backward and forward
questions.explanation: A palindrome is a word, phrase, or sequence that reads the same backward as forward. Examples include 'racecar', 'level', and 'noon'.

questions.question: What does 'ephemeral' mean?
choices: Lasting for a very short time
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time; transitory. It describes something that is short-lived or temporary.

questions.question: What does 'eloquent' mean?
choices: Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing
questions.explanation: Eloquent means fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing. An eloquent person expresses themselves clearly and effectively.

questions.question: What is a 'homophone'?
choices: A word that sounds the same as another but has different spelling
A word with the same spelling
questions.explanation: A homophone is a word that sounds the same as another word but has a different meaning and often different spelling. Examples: 'their/there/they're' or 'to/too/two'.

questions.question: What does 'benevolent' mean?
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly; showing goodwill and kindness. It describes someone who wishes to do good or help others.

questions.question: What does 'pragmatic' mean?
questions.explanation: Pragmatic means dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a practical way. A pragmatic approach focuses on what works rather than on theories.
